beats.text: Before you can know the world, Bacon said, you must face how badly your own mind distorts it.
He named four illusions — idols — that quietly warp our thinking.
Idols of the Tribe: human nature itself, seeing patterns and purpose where there are none.
Idols of the Cave: your private quirks — upbringing, favourite ideas — the lens only you look through.
Idols of the Marketplace: words themselves, sloppy language tricking us into muddled thought.
Idols of the Theatre: inherited dogmas and grand systems we accept like actors reciting a script.
Only by hunting these idols in yourself, he said, can you test the world instead of your own reflection.

source_note: From Novum Organum (1620, public-domain translation) — paraphrased.
